newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks in london listless, politics weigh.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks in london listless, politics weigh.

text.p: Japanese stocks trading in London were largely inactive on Tuesday following range-bound trade in Tokyo, where all eyes are turned to the new Japanese government and the U.S. presidential elections, dealers said.
In London, the Nikkei/Ise 50 index was off 3.11 points at 1,414.09 by 1505 GMT.
Tokyo stocks closed lower on Tuesday in a spiritless session ahead of the U.S. elections and prior to the launch of a new Japanese government. The Nikkei-225 fell 40.73 points to 20,592.33.

"The market is very dull in Tokyo, we seem to be stuck in a very tight trading range," one dealer said. "There's local political uncertainty and people are also waiting to see the impact of the U.S. election on the dollar."
Traders said Japanese shares are unlikely to make much progress over the next few days but when they do, domestic features could set the trend.
"There are still plenty of earnings coming out and they will eventually provide the direction," a trader said, adding that trading volumes were thin today.
Dealers noted some interest in bank stocks, particularly in Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd, which was trading at 2,310 yen in London, after a Tokyo close of 2,300 yen.
"There has been some positive news on the stock recently which didn't really get the follow-through in Tokyo," one dealer said. The bank recently added 60 percent to its interim profit forecast.
Elsewhere, profit-taking was noted in NEC, which was trading at 1,260 yen in London after finishing at 1,270 in Japan.
